A1.justification: Both PDFs describe KVComm and retain matching methods, experiments, and analyses. Inspection of all 20 pages of v1 and 27 pages of v2, including appendices, tables, figures, and equations, supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original communication experiments across eight model pairs, hidden-state interventions, layer-selection ablations, calibration experiments, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds extended evaluations, memory measurements, multiple-sender experiments, online calibration, and positional-alignment ablations.

M1.justification: The central attention/Gaussian scoring, top-M selection, and KV integration remain unchanged. Appendices J and L add bounded procedural extensions: aggregating KV information from multiple senders and recomputing selected layers every T queries. Newly documented positional offsets do not establish a change to the original implementation.

E1.justification: v2 adds SAMSum dialogue summarization, two-sender communication, and mixed-task streams for online calibration in Appendices E, J, and L. These expand task and input-environment coverage. The larger HotpotQA, QASPER, and MuSiQuest evaluations retain existing task coverage rather than introducing new datasets in substance.

E2.justification: The established comparison methods remain Baseline, Skyline, NLD, CIPHER, and the three AC variants; random and contiguous-layer comparisons are retained. Appendix M newly evaluates KVComm-S, a positional-reset comparison variant. Changed NLD/CIPHER scores do not establish a change in comparator identity or procedure.

E3.justification: Alongside the retained 500-example evaluations, v2 adds evaluations with 7,405 HotpotQA, 1,726 QASPER, and 2,417 MuSiQuest examples, plus a ninth model pair. New protocols vary NLD token budgets and recalibration intervals and measure memory. Figure 8 changes its reporting basis from per 128 input tokens to per query.

E4.justification: v2 retains the original selection, attention, calibration-size, and contiguous-layer studies. It adds NLD token-length sensitivity, one-versus-two-sender comparisons, online-calibration frequency tests, cross-dataset layer-ranking correlations, and positional-coherence ablations in Appendices I, J, L, and M. These substantially broaden the design questions examined.

E5.justification: Neither version documents repeated-run counts or seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added results retain point-estimate reporting; the new ranking correlations do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: NLD and CIPHER scores change extensively in Table 1 and v1 Table 6/v2 Table 8, while retained KVComm scores remain unchanged. For the first Table 1 model pair, HotpotQA NLD changes from 0.18 to 0.43 and CIPHER from 0.09 to 0.50. Their cause is unexplained. Substantial additional results cover extended evaluations, new analyses, and memory consumption.

T1.justification: Appendix J adds a mathematical generalization of attention scoring and KV concatenation to multiple senders. The original selection objective and computational-complexity derivations remain unchanged, with the detailed complexity analysis relocated from Appendix H to N. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same principal claims: selective non-contiguous KV sharing, calibration with one example, performance comparable to Skyline, and communication/computation savings. Added experiments and memory findings do not materially redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the broad debate-failure explanation with a distinction between salient-information tasks and complex contextual reasoning. New Section 6 and appendix discussions explain architectural compatibility, bandwidth constraints, calibration adaptability, prior-selection tradeoffs, positional coherence, and multi-agent scaling limits. This substantially expands interpretation and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/data access link and a reproducibility statement reporting release of code and synthetic datasets. Appendices C.1, D.1, and K specify hidden-state masking, prepending procedures, and receiver positional offsets. These substantially improve implementation disclosure; the previously stated hardware, precision, and principal hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds a substantive comparison with Ye et al. (2025)'s distinct, anchor-based KVComm and refines the DroidSpeak comparison. References also add Gliwa et al. for SAMSum and Jin et al. for communication-cost discussion. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence are retained. v2 makes localized clarifications and paragraph revisions, adds Discussion, Acknowledgments, and Reproducibility sections, and subdivides Appendices C and D into procedure and results subsections. The expansion does not constitute extensive rewriting of the existing paper.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6, 7, 10, and 11 and Figures 12–14, substantially expanding the visual presentation. Figure 8 is redrawn with memory measurements and revised FLOP scaling, while Figures 1, 3, and 10 receive clearer labels. Existing appendix displays are retained and relocated, including v1 Figure 12 becoming v2 Figure 15.

improvement.justification: The larger evaluations strengthen generalization checks, the NLD token-budget study addresses a concrete comparison concern, and implementation details, access information, and limitations improve reproducibility and interpretation. These provide a clear benefit over v1. However, substantial NLD/CIPHER score revisions remain unexplained, and the new multi-sender discussion generalizes too broadly from mixed Table 10 outcomes. These weaknesses limit the overall improvement.
